summary:
VORTIQRA – Outpost Commander is an interactive, browser-based educational simulation built with Next.js, React, JavaScript, and Tailwind CSS that places students in command of a lunar or Martian outpost.

Sustaining human life beyond Earth requires managing interconnected systems where one poor decision impacts the entire settlement, yet students rarely get practical, hands-on exposure to these trade-offs. VORTIQRA addresses this challenge by having users manage seven essential outpost indicators—oxygen, water, food, power, shielding, crew health, and morale—through staged mission scenarios. Featuring a Mission Control Dashboard, decision-based gameplay, real-time scientific explanations, and mission reviews, the simulation introduces core space concepts like Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS), In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), energy conservation, and sustainable habitat operations.

This project is important because it shifts learners from passive reading to active decision-making, fostering critical thinking, systems awareness, and STEM engagement. (Note: All resource changes use simplified educational values, not real NASA engineering or operational data.)
details:
VORTIQRA – OUTPOST COMMANDER

Challenge: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer
Event: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
Project Category: Space Exploration, Educational Simulation, and Interactive Learning
Team Name: VORTIQRA
Team Leader: Vikram Heerani

Project Description

VORTIQRA – Outpost Commander is an interactive educational simulation that allows users to experience the responsibilities of managing a lunar or Martian outpost. Users take the role of an outpost commander and make important decisions involving oxygen, water, food, power, shielding, crew health, and morale.

The project transforms complex space exploration concepts into an engaging, mission-based learning experience. Through an interactive Mission Control dashboard and decision-based scenarios, users can observe how their choices affect the simulated condition of an extraterrestrial settlement.

Problem We Address

Future human settlements beyond Earth will require careful resource management, reliable life-support systems, sustainable energy, and effective crew management. Students may understand these concepts theoretically but have limited opportunities to explore how these systems interact in practical situations.

Our Solution

VORTIQRA provides a simulated outpost environment where users face mission challenges, evaluate different strategies, manage limited resources, and learn from the outcomes of their decisions.

Key Features

  • Interactive Mission Control dashboard
  • Oxygen, water, food, and power monitoring
  • Crew health, morale, and shielding indicators
  • Decision-based mission scenarios
  • Scientific explanations and educational feedback
  • Mission progression and resource management

Scientific Concepts

The project introduces Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS), In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), sustainable resource management, and extraterrestrial habitat operations.

Technology Stack

Next.js, React, JavaScript, and Tailwind CSS.

Expected Impact

VORTIQRA aims to make space science more accessible, encourage critical thinking and problem-solving, and inspire students to explore STEM subjects and future space exploration.

Project Vision

To help learners understand the challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth through interactive simulation and scientific learning.

Tagline: Command the Outpost. Master the Mission. Explore Beyond Earth.
